answer: Use "spiral handshake" as the mechanism. Each identity must complete a timed round-trip through a spiral of randomly selected relays, where the echo of its own signed nonce returns within a narrow window. Real operators pay a fixed hardware latency per hop, so an attacker running many clones must replicate that delay on dedicated physical links, costing roughly one rented relay per identity. Identities also post an onyx token locked to their relay’s clock drift; cloning forces fresh drift signatures each cycle, raising the per-identity cost to a metered line rental plus calibration.
